valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull values of four equity methods 30/50/20 (about 0.71x NAV). No cash-flow DCF: a finance company's deposits and bank loans are its raw material, so it is valued on equity. All four methods are computed by scripts/valuation.py. The same fair value applies to the non-voting share (same dividend and profit share).

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: NAV Rs 40.34 × (long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 12% / 16% / 19%, growth 5% / 6% / 7%, cost of equity 19.7% / 18.2% / 16.7% (0.48x / 0.82x / 1.24x book).

models.name: P/E on normal earnings
models.comment: 2026/27 EPS of Rs 4.80 / 5.60 / 6.30 at the justified forward P/E (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g): 4.0x / 5.1x / 6.5x. Base EPS is 6% below the Rs 5.96 run-rate (H1 × 2 is Rs 5.52, and Q2 profit fell 25%); bear 19% below, for rising bad loans and funding costs.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Rs 1.50 / 1.75 / 2.00 next year, growing 4% / 7% / 9% (below the supported 12.4%) for five years; then EPS grows at 5% / 6% / 7% with the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE (58% / 63% / 63%), at the cost of equity. Lowest of the four because today's payout is only 28%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF: book Rs 40.34 plus profit above the 18.2% required return; ROE moves from 14% now to 12% / 16% / 19% over five years, 28% payout, then excess returns grow at 5% / 6% / 7%. ROE below the cost of equity destroys value, so the base is under book.

summary.headline: A fast-growing lender whose returns and loan quality slipped this half: fair value Rs 28.50, buy at Rs 24.20 or lower
summary.text: Citizens Development Business Finance (CDB.N0000) is a Colombo-based leasing and loans finance company, about 34% owned by Ceylinco Life. At Rs 32.50 (30 September last trade) it trades at 0.81x NAV of Rs 40.34, 5.5x trailing earnings and yields 5.4% on the Rs 1.75 dividend for 2025/26. 2025/26 was a big growth year: loans up 53% to Rs 169bn, profit up 12% to Rs 4.5bn (EPS Rs 6.28, ROE 17.2%) and gross bad loans down to 3.78%. The September half-year shows the cost of that growth: interest expense up 56% against interest income up 35%, the margin down from 7.10% to 6.37%, profit down 9% to Rs 2.0bn (Q2 down 25%), ROE down to 13.9%, and gross non-performing loans up from 3.78% to 6.01%. Core capital is 12.1% against a 10% minimum. Using the site's standard required return (18.2%, from a 0.97 finance-sector beta) and a long-run ROE of 16%, four equity methods give a fair value of Rs 28.47, about 12% below the price. I'd buy at Rs 24.20 or lower and treat Rs 21.35 as a strong buy. The business passes three of four tests (returns over five years, capital above the minimums, cash dividends) but profit isn't steady, so it goes on the watch list.

fullText:
Summary: Citizens Development Business Finance (CDB.N0000) is a Colombo-based licensed finance company (leasing and loans) with Rs 234bn of assets, about 34% owned by Ceylinco Life. At Rs 32.50 (30 September 2026 last trade) it trades at 0.81x NAV of Rs 40.34 and 5.5x trailing earnings, and yields 5.4%. My fair value is Rs 28.47; buy at Rs 24.20 or lower, strong buy at Rs 21.35. It passes three of four business tests, so it goes on the watch list: a good business at too high a price after a weaker half-year.

**What happened**
2025/26 was a year of fast growth. Loans grew 53% to Rs 169.2bn, profit rose 12% to Rs 4.51bn (EPS Rs 6.28 after the April 2026 one-for-ten split), ROE was 17.21% and gross non-performing loans fell from 6.32% to 3.78%. Most of the growth was funded by bank borrowing, which rose from Rs 32.1bn to Rs 77.3bn, while deposits rose only 5%.

The six months to September 2026 show the cost. Interest expense rose 56% against interest income up 35%, so net interest income rose only 14% and the margin fell to 6.37%. Profit fell 9% to Rs 2.00bn (EPS Rs 2.76), with the second quarter down 25%. Gross non-performing loans rose to Rs 11.2bn (6.01%), provision cover fell to 37%, and core capital fell to 12.14% (minimum 10%).

**Valuation (Rs per share, bear / base / bull, weighted 30/50/20)**
- Justified price to book: 19.21 / 33.07 / 49.91 → 32.28
- P/E on normal earnings: 19.05 / 28.69 / 41.02 → 28.26
- Dividend model: 14.35 / 23.40 / 36.13 → 23.23
- Residual income: 17.27 / 30.46 / 48.55 → 30.12
Average of the four: Rs 28.47.

**Assumptions**
Cost of equity 19.7% / 18.2% / 16.7% (risk-free 8.24% + beta 0.97 × 10.28%). Long-run ROE 12% / 16% / 19%: the company earned 9–23% over five years, 17.2% last year and 13.9% this half. Long-run growth 5% / 6% / 7%, below the 12.24% bond yield. 2026/27 EPS Rs 4.80 / 5.60 / 6.30 against a Rs 5.96 run-rate. Next dividend Rs 1.50 / 1.75 / 2.00 growing 4% / 7% / 9%; 72% of profit kept × 17.2% ROE supports 12.4% growth, so every case is within it.

The key point: with ROE around 14–16% and a required return of 18.2%, the business earns less than shareholders should demand, so it is worth less than book. The price implies a long-run ROE of about 16.6%.

**Business tests (3 of 4)**
- Returns: pass, on a five-year average of about 16%, but falling (13.9% this half).
- Capital: pass, core capital 12.14% and total 16.08% against minimums of 10% and 14%, but the buffer is narrowing.
- Steady profit: fail; profit fell 55% in 2022/23 and Q2 2026/27 is down 25%.
- Cash and dividends: pass; Rs 1.75 a share paid in cash.

**Buy plan (500 shares)**
150 at Rs 28.47 or less, 200 at Rs 24.20 or less, 150 at Rs 21.35 or less: about Rs 12,300 in total. This year's low was Rs 32.30, so the buy price needs a 26% fall. The non-voting share (CDB.X0000, Rs 29.00) gets the same dividend at an 11% discount and has no vote.

**Management**
The Chairman and CEO say the focus now shifts from scale to profitability and ROE, with a quarter-trillion balance sheet in 2026/27, more retail deposits and an AI roadmap. The balance sheet target is on track (Rs 234.5bn), but asset quality, which they presented as improving, got worse in the half, and ROE fell.

**What would change my view**
Higher: bad loans back towards 4%, the margin back above 7%, ROE above 17%. Lower: bad loans above 6%, a rights issue, tighter vehicle lending rules slowing growth.

**Uncertain**
The price is the 30 September last trade, because the CSE feed couldn't be reached from this run; the site will show the latest close. The beta is a sector figure (no local 5-year betas found).
